#Tesla closed yesterday at $350.25 and is trading today below the key $348.16 support level, putting the stock under immediate pressure.

*

About five to six weeks ago, #TSLA closed below the bottom of its 18-month rising channel at $382.73, triggering a longer-term sell signal with a $228.24 target over the following 3–5 months.

That bearish structure remains intact, but a counter-trend rally was expected after Tesla tested the low $290s — and that rally has played out.

The key question now is whether it can continue.

*

$348.16 is key to the continuation of this counter-trend rally.

Yesterday’s close above it technically preserved bullish momentum, but today’s move below it puts the rally at risk. A break of this level alone isn’t confirmation; today's settlement matters.

*

If $TSLA reclaims and holds $348.16, the counter-trend rally remains healthy.

The next important resistance is $362.86, followed by rising channel resistance around $370.54. A push through those levels keeps $382.73 in play over the next week or two.

*

But a settlement below $348.16 changes the near-term picture.

It would suggest that Tesla may have already established a good high for August and puts $340.10, the 3/8 downside Fibonacci level, in play first.

Below that, $328.78 becomes the next major target. That represents the 5/8 downside Fibonacci retracement of the recent move.

A confirmed break of $348.16 could ultimately send Tesla back into the low $290s over the following 2–5 weeks.

*

The bigger-picture bearish thesis remains centered on $382.73.

That level begins a major long-term resistance zone extending to $416.03.

As long as Tesla remains below this zone, the original $228.24 downside target remains active.
